subject: VoiceMem second-pass hidden failure lessons after full-tree empirical-marker audit

routes.use: zero-activation/dead-path telemetry; effective-config receipts; latency span attribution
schema-generation migration compatibility and fail-closed read adapters
deferred completion visibility/re-entry rather than hidden asynchronous gaps
update-candidate recall and read-time relevance without lifecycle mutation
calibration and uncertainty; confidence score alone is not epistemic reliability
speaker/presence freshness trade-offs and cross-identity isolation
event-loop nonblocking architecture, realtime effective-config validation, per-response state delivery
micro-world regression fixtures for all delta mechanisms
lesion tests for dead graph path/config omission
failure injection: legacy schema row, silent config reject, queue/visibility race

new_findings.source_observation: cognitive_graph/store.py documents a live bug where SlotV2(row['slot']) raised on legacy taxonomy rows such as slot='people'. One bad row propagated through find_entities/get_entity and AnchorRouter, silently zeroing all right-brain results for the user. The repair coerces known legacy values and falls back to knowledge rather than crashing the entire query.
new_findings.general_lesson: A local schema-generation incompatibility must not create whole-user/whole-subsystem retrieval failure. Read paths require explicit generation migration or typed UNKNOWN/legacy handling.
new_findings.counterhypothesis: Fallback coercion can hide genuinely invalid data and silently misclassify it.
new_findings.cheapest_discriminator: Inject one known-legacy row and one unknown-invalid row into a compatibility fixture. Known legacy must migrate deterministically with receipt; unknown must become typed UNKNOWN/BLOCKED or isolated error, never silently poison the full query and never be treated as trusted knowledge.

new_findings.source_observation: neighbor_entity_ids had SQL placeholder ordering wrong; donor comments state one-hop neighbor expansion never worked and an evaluation over 821 questions had f_nbr=0 throughout. The surrounding pipeline could still run, making the feature appear present while causally dead.
new_findings.general_lesson: Source presence and green outer-path execution do not prove a cognitive branch ever contributes. Every intended adaptive/graph/GWT branch needs activation-count and causal-contribution telemetry.
new_findings.counterhypothesis: A branch can legitimately remain zero on a dataset where its trigger condition never occurs.
new_findings.cheapest_discriminator: Add a positive-control fixture guaranteed to require the branch plus runtime activation counters. Acceptance requires nonzero branch activation on positive controls and zero on explicit negative controls; do not infer usefulness merely from activation.

new_findings.source_observation: Graph edges and memory heat are exponentially decayed at read time while stored base weights remain unchanged. Archivable-memory listing only proposes candidates; execution is a separate caller action with minimum-age protection.
new_findings.general_lesson: Freshness/relevance decay can be a rebuildable query projection rather than destructive canonical-state mutation. Candidate archival must remain distinct from archive effect.
new_findings.counterhypothesis: Read-time decay tied to wall clock harms deterministic replay unless reference time is explicit.
new_findings.cheapest_discriminator: Require explicit reference_time in deterministic F2 analogues; replay identical state+reference_time to identical score and verify no canonical payload/lifecycle mutation occurs.

new_findings.source_observation: web/run.py keeps a short-lived _LAST_TUNE cache because background ingest can take 15-20 seconds; a natural immediate request to replay the just-heard song arrives before its durable memory is query-visible. The transient buffer bridges that gap without pretending durable ingest completed.
new_findings.general_lesson: Asynchronous cognition/persistence creates a consistency window. Immediate re-entry needs an explicit pending/provisional visibility layer rather than forcing synchronous durable ingest or pretending the write is complete.
new_findings.counterhypothesis: A transient cache can become a second truth source or leak stale data after ingest failure.
new_findings.cheapest_discriminator: Model PENDING -> DURABLE|FAILED with exact causal id and TTL. Immediate same-session query may see typed PENDING evidence; after durable receipt it resolves to canonical ref; after failure/TTL it disappears. Never grant durable-memory credit from the provisional layer.

new_findings.source_observation: web/run.py documents emotion2vec+ confidently wrong at score 1.00 on benign real utterances. Raising a numeric confidence threshold could not solve the error; VoiceMem instead restricts trust to selected acoustically distinctive classes and uses semantic evidence elsewhere.
new_findings.general_lesson: A model's internal confidence score is not evidence of calibration. Admission policy must be class/condition-specific or externally calibrated, and disagreement should remain UNKNOWN/Hyperposition rather than be collapsed by high self-confidence.
new_findings.counterhypothesis: The observed miscalibration may be speaker/domain-specific and class allowlists may overfit one user.
new_findings.cheapest_discriminator: Held-out multi-speaker calibration set; reliability diagram/ECE or bounded calibration metric by class. Compare global threshold, class-conditional gate and multimodal disagreement policy.

new_findings.source_observation: web/run.py documents a synchronous speaker/perception read taking about 2.1 seconds inside the event loop; during it the socket was not read and microphone frames accumulated, perceived as ASR lag. Barge-in was also structurally impossible while reply generation/TTS was awaited inline; repair moved reply work to cancellable background task while socket consumption continued.
new_findings.general_lesson: Realtime agency must classify scheduler/event-loop starvation separately from model latency. Long perception/cognition cannot block ingress or interrupt handling.
new_findings.counterhypothesis: Moving work off the event loop can create stale prior-state decisions and races.
new_findings.cheapest_discriminator: Inject bounded slow perception/reply tasks while streaming input. Measure socket/read-loop gap, queued audio growth, barge-in latency, cancellation completion and stale-generation rejection.

new_findings.source_observation: Realtime turn_detection was previously written at the wrong schema level and silently rejected through an error event; code behaved as if server VAD were disabled when it was not. This caused auto-responses without injected memory and collisions with the client's response.create. The current source places turn_detection under session.audio.input and treats handshake success as insufficient until interaction works.
new_findings.general_lesson: Configuration request != effective configuration. Provider/runtime setup requires an observed acknowledgement/effective-state receipt, and error events must be consumed.
new_findings.counterhypothesis: Provider schemas and acknowledgements can change; one success does not prove future effective state.
new_findings.cheapest_discriminator: Negative fixture with an intentionally invalid nested config must produce BLOCKED/REJECTED receipt, never READY. Positive fixture must bind requested config digest to observed effective/accepted response before dependent runtime credit.

new_findings.source_observation: VoiceMem comments report session.update instructions were not visible to the current response even though memory had been retrieved; moving memory context into per-response response.create instructions made it available to that response.
new_findings.general_lesson: State/config existence at session scope does not prove delivery to the exact consuming inference. Bind context to the concrete model-call/response identity when current-turn causality matters.
new_findings.counterhypothesis: Per-call context can increase duplication/token cost.
new_findings.cheapest_discriminator: Two-turn fixture with changing memory context. Require exact call receipt showing context digest consumed by intended response; compare session-scoped vs call-scoped delivery and token overhead.

new_findings.source_observation: voice_input.py documents a reproduced household bug where a current speaker's new fact updated another named person's similar old memory despite a prompt rule. The repair hard-filters candidates explicitly naming another known person before the model conflict resolver sees them.
new_findings.general_lesson: Identity/authority boundaries cannot rely on prompt instructions. Candidate construction must hard-fence principal/subject identity before a model may propose UPDATE/DELETE-like actions.
new_findings.counterhypothesis: Name filtering alone is brittle under aliases/coreference or shared facts.
new_findings.cheapest_discriminator: Multi-principal fixture with same-template facts, aliases and shared entities; a candidate updater must not receive foreign-principal mutable candidates without explicit cross-principal relation evidence.

new_findings.source_observation: VoiceMem changed conflict resolution from one whole-turn top-10 search to per-fact wider search plus an attribute-only query. Source comments explain that different values of the same attribute can be embedding-dissimilar, causing old values to miss top-k and turning intended UPDATE into ADD.
new_findings.general_lesson: Candidate retrieval for state reconciliation has different recall requirements from answer retrieval. It should query stable relation/attribute identity in addition to value-bearing text.
new_findings.counterhypothesis: Wider candidate windows increase latency and false conflict risk; donor comments report one conflict-resolver call took 10.2s with a 95-memory store.
new_findings.cheapest_discriminator: Ablate whole-turn top-k, per-fact top-k and per-attribute candidate retrieval on update/delete recall, false-conflict rate, prompt size and latency. Keep effect/mutation downstream separately gated.

new_findings.source_observation: voice_input.py has an optional raw-text memory fallback for extraction failure/offline use but leaves it disabled by default; otherwise unstructured request/junk can be persisted as if it were quality-extracted memory.
new_findings.general_lesson: Degraded fallback modes must change epistemic type, not silently preserve the normal success label.
new_findings.counterhypothesis: Failing closed can lose valuable user information during provider outage.
new_findings.cheapest_discriminator: If a raw fallback is ever admitted, store it as RAW_OBSERVATION/PENDING_EXTRACTION with separate retrieval policy and later reconciliation; verify it cannot appear as FACT until typed admission succeeds.

worker_priority: P0: positive-control activation telemetry for graph/GWT/adaptive branches (VM-F02)
P0: provisional PENDING visibility/read-your-own-writes contract without second truth authority (VM-F04)
P0 runtime: nonblocking ingress/barge-in and effective-config receipts (VM-F06/F07/F08)
P1: typed raw fallback if degraded/offline operation is required (VM-F11)
